title: CDF governance audit event
description: One line of the append-only governance journal. Rotated files carry the same shape. Deliberately holds a request hash rather than the request, and a sanitised summary rather than content: this file is retained indefinitely, so anything that reaches it is effectively permanent. CORRECTED against real artefacts: event_id and session_id are NOT required. A writer active between 2026-05-12 and 2026-05-15 emitted 61 codex.health.audit_probe records without them. The journal is append-only and retained indefinitely, so those records are permanent and a conformant reader will meet them. Rejecting real evidence would be worse than a slightly weaker schema. The current writer emits both.

event_id.description: Optional for historical reasons only — see the schema description. Current writers emit it.

event_type.description: OPEN, unlike the CDI signal vocabulary. The journal records what happened; a product may record its own kinds of event.

session_id.description: Optional for historical reasons only — see the schema description. Current writers emit it.

phase.description: An OPEN string. This field previously carried a closed six-value software lifecycle union, which meant a product with a different lifecycle could not record its own phase in the shared journal without lying. A reader must tolerate an unrecognised value: not throw, not coerce it to a known one, not drop it.

actor.description: Who or what acted. Records the KIND of actor and the model, never a person's name, email or git identity.

request_hash.description: SHA-256 of the request. NEVER the request itself.

details.description: Sanitised before write: keys matching token, secret, password, authorization, prompt, content, file or path are dropped. Do not defeat this by renaming a sensitive field.
